text.p: Hanson Plc, acknowledging its poor share price performance, said on Thursday that the share price "in no way represents either our earnings capacity or future prospects."
Hanson Plc, in the throes of splitting into separate companies, reported its last full set of full group results on Thursday.

Founder Lord Hanson said in the results statement, The performance of the share price is of over-riding importance to all shareholders and has been very disappointing. The combined value of Hanson and the demerged companies was 195p on December 1, 1995 and now stands at 150p."
He said, "This in no way represents either our earning capacity or future prospects."

"Hanson's profit in each of the last five years has comfortably exceeded one billion stg and this year's result shows clearly that the momentum continues. All your demerged companies are completely focused on profitability and while we do not control the stock markets, we shall do for you what we've done for over 30 years...keep making excellent profits," Lord Hanson told shareholders in the results statement.
Hanson earlier reported pre-tax profit of 1.81 billion stg for the year ended October 1, including exceptional gains of 609 million.
